title: Theatre Review A Game Of Inches

display_heading.headline: A Game of Inches comes up short
display_heading.deck: In her latest solo turn, actress and writer Linda Griffiths presents a concoction that's too elaborate to be a comedy and too sketchy to cut it as a play

body_presentation.source_prefix:
THEATRE REVIEW A GAME OF INCHES

Saturday, March 16, 1991

ROBERT CUSHMAN

WRITTEN BY AND STARRING LINDA GRIFFITHS Directed by Sandra Balcovske At Theatre Passe Muraille Mainspace, in Toronto In her latest solo turn, actress and writer Linda Griffiths presents a concoction that's too elaborate to be a comedy and too sketchy to cut it as a play A Game of Inches comes up short BY ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail IHAVE only seen one previous Linda Griffiths show, the embarrassingly amateurish Maggie and Pierre. I know it's considered a landmark in Canadian theatre, but so much the worse for Canadian theatre. I recall a smug endless monologue that was tickled pink by its own daring at lampooning the First Couple, and laid itself in the aisles at the audacity of having both of them done by the same actor. Since that actor's sole idea of characterization was to portray everyone as Barbra Streisand joke-Jewish, jabbing nasally at anything that resembled a comic point, the notion palled rather quickly.
